contact_edits.before: The production is slapdash in some of its other choices. Duke Frederick subjects Oliver to a waterboarding, that being the most topical of tortures; too much dialogue is underscored by the splashing of water or the bleating of lambs, and by both at once at one crucial point. I don't see why "the second son of old Sir Rowland" shouldn't be allowed to announce himself as such when he makes his last-minute appearance; coincidence and Shakespearean comedy are hardly strangers. But the ancestral, eye-pricking magic that lies within this play is fully released in the multiple pairings at the end. Soulpepper has yet to offer us a great Shakespeare production, but this is their best try yet. - As You Like It runs in repertory until April 19 at the Young Centre for Performing Arts, Toronto. Call 416-866-8666 for tickets and information.
